brief: The near block's roof is the biggest thing in the picture and the least detailed thing in it. Measured on HEAD at midsummer midday, it is ~21% of a 1600x950 frame and ~24% of a 390x844 one, and its horizontal luma variance is sd 4.6-11 against sd 21-35 for the town behind it — falling as the pitch comes TOWARD the viewer (sd 21.9 at the parapet, 4.6 four fifths of the way down). The cause is in `drawRoofRow`: our own block is painted one flat quad per grid CELL, tinted by a single `hash(gx,y)` through `tileCol`, with a course line only at each row boundary and the down-joint deliberately suppressed (`if (y < LN_WALK_S)`) — on a phone that is a quad ~6 px wide and ~37 px tall, which is why it reads as vertical boarding rather than slate. Four iterations have worked this roof's edges and its tenants and none has touched its surface, and #123 proved nothing TALL can be added: between the parapet and the shortest framing's sill there is 2.55 of depth and a water tank is 2.549 of it. So retire the flat fill and build a real slated roof: courses at SLATE scale rather than grid scale, with staggered laps and per-slate value variance, and then let the surface AGE — lichen and moss where the pitch is damp and in the parapet's shade, soot below the stacks, the odd slipped or replaced slate, snow lying course by course. This is the ladder's rung 6 and the swing is the point: a 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome.
successLooksLike: At 1600x950 and 390x844 on a dry midsummer midday, horizontal luma sd across the near roof's band is at least the town's own (>= 20) and no longer falls toward the viewer; the band's changed-pixel share against HEAD is >= 60% on a difference image whose same-code control floor is near 0; and at thirty seconds a visitor reads the foreground as a slate roof rather than as boarding — while the town still reads PAST it.
avoid: Do NOT put new objects on the roof: that band is #110's and #123's and it is full to six thousandths of a cell. Do NOT raise the band's mean luma — the composition depends on the foreground being the dark thing (the comment above SLATES says so), so more detail must not mean a brighter roof. Leave ROOF_FURN placement, the parapet geometry and the dormers alone. `drawNearRoof` is inside the GROUND CACHE, so this is cache-time cost: measure with frame-cost.mjs, not perf.mjs, and if the sub-cell loop is dear, scale slates-per-cell with cellW rather than dropping the feature at small sizes.
